DATE  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE  FIR/ORDER) NO. 1663 of 2025  ==========================================================
 AMITKUMAR RAJUBHAI BAMANIYA & ANR.
 Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR PRADIP J PATEL(5896) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2  A R KADRI(7330) for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR JK SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP N. BHATT  Date : 10/02/2025  ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned advocates waive service of rule for respective respondents.
2. With the consent of learned advocates for the parties, present application is taken up for final disposal today.
The victim is present and has tendered copy of the affidavit, which is taken on record.

3. By way of the present petition under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (`BNSS' for short), the applicant prays for quashing and setting aside the F.I.R. being C.R.No.11207024240451 of 2024 registered with Godhra Taluka Police Station, Panchmahal for the offences under the provisions of the IPC and POCSO Act mentioned therein.

4. Learned advocate for the applicant has taken this Court through the factual matrix arising out of the present application.
5. It is now stated at bar that the applicant and the victim have settled the dispute amicably and the victim has no grievance against the applicant.
Not only that, the victim and the applicant have married each other.
Learned advocate Mr.Kadri for respondent no.1-complainant opposed this petition and submits that the respondent no.2-complainant, who is the mother of the victim, is not agreeable for the consent.

6. However, as the victim is major and she has tendered the affidavit to the effect that she is married with the applicant and she is not interested to proceed with the proceedings anymore, the impugned FIR is required to be quashed, as otherwise, their marital life will be put into jeopardize.

7. It is now settled that in serious offence as one u/s 376 of the IPC and under the provisions of the POCSO Act cannot be subject matter of quashment of the proceedings initiated u/s 528 of the BNSS on the ground of settlement between the accused and the victim.

Suffice it to refer the various decisions rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court on such aspect, more particularly, in cases of Anita Maria Dias Vs. State of Maharashtra reported in (2018) 3 SCC 290, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1663/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/02/2025 undefined Shimbu Vs. State of Haryana reported in (2014) 13 SCC 318 and Parbatbhai Ahir Vs. State of Gujarat reported in (2017) 9 SCC 641.

sentences.text: However, this Court cannot overlook the fact that the applicant and the victim girl got married.

Such situation is an exception to the approach to deal with the proceedings initiated u/s 528 of the BNSS on the basis of settlement between the victim and the accused and for the pre-dominant purpose of the welfare of the victim to ensure her better future life, it is just and proper for this Court in exercise of extraordinary inherent powers u/s 528 of the BNSS could quash the impugned criminal proceedings on the ground of settlement between the parties in cases where the accused has married the victim and the victim insist for quashment of impugned criminal proceedings.

8. It will be fruitful to refer to the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 21.3.2022 passed in Criminal Appeal No.456 of 2022, wherein it is observed and held as under:
"Leave granted.

An FIR was lodged against the appellant by the respondent no.2 for offences under Sections 417, 420 and 376 IPC alleging that the respondent no.2 was introduced to the petitioner through Bharat Matrimony and thereafter they remained in touch with each other.
It was alleged that on the promise to marry, the appellant made physical relationship with relationship no.2.
Thereafter, since the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1663/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/02/2025 undefined appellant refused to marry, the FIR was lodged by the respondent no.2.
However, it is not disputed that on 23.09.2020, the appellant and the respondent no.2 have got married, for which marriage certificate has also been issued on the same date.

sentences.text: The appellant then filed an application for quashing of the FIR.
The High Court dismissed the petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

Aggrieved by the said order,
this appeal by way of special leave petition has been filed.
On earlier occasion, this Court directed the respondent no.2 to be present through video-conferencing.

Today,
respondent no.2, namely, Ms.T.Harshini appeared through video- conferencing, who has been duly identified by Mr.Saivamshi V., learned counsel.

Respondent no.2 has made a statement that it is correct that she is now married to the appellant and leading a happy married life and has also made a statement that she does not wish to press the FIR lodged against the appellant.

Considering the aforesaid facts and keeping in view that the respondent no.2/complainant has herself made a statement before us that she has married the appellant and now living happily, we exercise our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and to do complete justice in the matter, we quash the FIR dated 16.08.2020 lodged by the respondent no.2 against the appellant under Sections 417, 420 and 376 IPC.
The appeal stands allowed accordingly."
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1663/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/02/2025 undefined 9.

In view of the aforementioned aspect, more particularly, in light of the statements made by the victim supported by duly affirmed affidavit placed on record through their learned advocate, this Court is inclined to consider the plea for quashment of the impugned criminal proceedings, as otherwise, it will detrimentally affect the family life of the victim girl and even the balance and harmony that could be achieved by them in the resolution of disputes that again be irrecoverably lost.

10. Since now, the dispute with reference to the impugned F.I.R. is settled and resolved by and between parties which is confirmed by the victim through her learned advocate, the trial would be futile and any further continuation of proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.

Therefore, the impugned F.I.R. is required to be quashed and set aside in view of peculiar facts of the case being exception to the general principle of law to decline the quashment of proceedings of the nature like present one.
11. In view of this position, this application is allowed.
Impugned F.I.R. being C.R.No.11207024240451 of 2024 registered with Godhra Taluka Police Station, Panchmahal and all other proceedings, if any,
are hereby quashed and set aside.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) SRILATHA Amitkumar Rajubhai Bamaniya vs State Of Gujarat on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40114013/
